chapter.title: How to Awaken the Automatic Success Mechanism Within You

concepts.title: Built-in success instinct metaphor
concepts.content: The chapter presents purposeful human problem-solving as analogous to an organism pursuing survival and meaningful goals. Animals’ navigational and survival instincts are used as a bridge to a wider human goal-seeking system that includes creativity and fulfillment.

terms.definition: The chapter presents purposeful human problem-solving as analogous to an organism pursuing survival and meaningful goals.

concepts.author_mechanism: Animals’ navigational and survival instincts are used as a bridge to a wider human goal-seeking system that includes creativity and fulfillment.
concepts.conditions_and_limits: This is a book assertion and metaphor; reject claims of a guaranteed or literal internal success device.
concepts.application: Translate a vague wish into a goal you can observe and a next action within your control.
concepts.common_misreading: Treating a conceptual or anecdotal explanation as a universal causal law, without evaluating context, skills or competing explanations.
concepts.alternative_explanation: Biology, learning, motivation and cultural supports provide multiple explanations for goal pursuit.
concepts.ethical_clinical_cautions: This is a book assertion and metaphor; reject claims of a guaranteed or literal internal success device.

concepts.content: The servo metaphor distinguishes steering toward a known target from searching for an answer not yet known. One mechanism corrects course toward a target; another combines stored information to recognize a solution.

concepts.title: Negative feedback and iterative correction
concepts.content: Progress often requires detecting error, adjusting direction and continuing rather than interpreting an error as defeat. The guided torpedo and reaching-for-a-pencil examples illustrate small course corrections using sensory feedback.

evidence_assessments.title: Paranormal memory access
